item.title: Live Updates: Midterm voters go to the polls on Election Day
item.description:
Election day is finally here, and amid national chatter about the big blue wave, the balance of power in Congress could all come down to New York . No pressure, right? Early voting numbers have reportedly slowed since 2025, particularly in the Commie Corridor, which saw a 34 percent drop in early voting this election, but early voting increased in majority Black districts across the city , including Central Brooklyn (a 50 percent jump) and parts of Southeast Queens. (By the way, if you live in New York City and procrastinated on voting—and who would do something like that, especially if they had to work overtime on election night, ha ha ha— here's where to find your polling site .) Tonight, we will learn if North Country voters choose a dairy farming executive, Democrat Blake Gendebien, over a guy with an AI rap album that lobs Islamophobic slurs at Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Republican…

item.title: Russian strikes on Dnipro kill two, injure 20 others
item.description:
Teams of emergency workers and volunteers picked through debris at the cratered blast site in Komyshuvakha, a village in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region where bodies were pulled from the rubble and carried away in white plastic sheeting. More than 45 residents are still missing.

item.title: If Democrats Win, Thank the Left
item.description:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) walks with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) in May 2026 in Washington, DC. | Win McNamee/Getty Images The outcome of the midterm elections is perhaps the single most important factor in determining how the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency will play out — and what impact it will have on people’s lives in the United States and around the world. item.title: What Do Libertarians Have To Gain From the Midterms?
item.description:
This week, editors Peter Suderman , Katherine Mangu-Ward , Nick Gillespie , and Matt Welch discuss what the midterm elections could mean for libertarians. They debate whether a Democratic victory might help curb President Donald Trump's executive power and why Republicans may struggle to learn from their mistakes. The conversation then turns to races in Ohio, Alaska, and Michigan that reveal growing tensions within both parties. The editors then examine how much power Democrats would actually have if they retake Congress, particularly when it comes to Trump's tariffs and the war with Iran. They also weigh the value of congressional investigations against the risk of more political grandstanding. Finally, a listener's question about gerrymandering leads to a discussion of electoral reform and the possibility of expanding the House of Representatives. 0:00—What the midterms mean for…

item.title: Martha Stewart's Homeless Halloween Costume Was Perfect for Her
item.description:
Martha Stewart is poor. Didn't you know? She is homeless and filthy and hungry and has excellent taste in candles, which are now on sale . This is Halloween 2026, when one of the richest women on Earth—the world's first self-made female billionaire—dressed as a homeless woman, her face smudged with dirt, a sign beckoning for food. Hopefully help is on the way. The titan of home decor unveiled her costume in an Instagram carousel hawking her flameless Halloween candles, available on QVC. She is on brand even when off brand. The bit was short-lived. It quickly became a casualty of internet commentators, some of whom were not impressed by the delta between Stewart's wealth and the lack thereof held by those who live the reality she briefly cosplayed.
